newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher in volatile trade.

text.p: Bombay share prices shrugged off late profit-taking to finish higher on Friday but the outlook was undecided and undercurrent shaky, brokers said.
It was a day of fluctuating fortunes as punters booked profits as prices rose, and returned to cover their short-sold positions at the lower levels.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 38.72 points, or 1.24 percent, higher at a provisional 3,165.06 after moving between 3,121.95 and 3,176.97.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) gained 9.33 points, or 1.04 percent, to a provisional 907.33.
Traders said the market was expected to focus on first half company results for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) which will begin next week.
"The pivotals will lose charm," said Vijay Bhatia, chief dealer at broker Pashupati Advani. "No one's particularly bullish."
Top companies like steel, cement, capital goods and petrochemicals are expected to report sharp slowdown in earnings growth, analysts said.
Analysts were also awaiting direction from the central bank's credit policy for the second half of fiscal 1996/97.
The bank is expected to ease liquidity conditions when the policy is announced shortly.

Some shares were pushed by good corporate news. ABB rose 65.75 rupees, or 8.76 percent, to 816.25 after the electrical machinery firm said its board will meet on October 17 to consider interim dividend and bonus issue.
TELCO gained 13.50 rupees to 427, Bajaj Auto 23.75 to 937, Grasim 15 to 415, BHEL 9.50 to 181.75, Hind Lever 7.0 to 798.75 and TISCO 4.50 to 173.50.
SBI fell 4.0 to 213.75, Reliance 2.75 to 193, ITC 2.75 to 321 and Colgate 3.0 to 229.50.
